title: Ops Weave: Composable admin utility kit for runbooks-as-tasks
creator: Priya Nair
description: Build a lightweight composable library (Ops Weave) that lets oncall engineers and first-line support stitch small, typed admin actions (stitches) into safe runbooks-as-tasks. Ops Weave aims to: 1) standardize interfaces for atomic admin utilities; 2) provide preflight/dry-run and permission gates; 3) publish telemetry so Console can suggest replacements/optimizations; and 4) enable safe automated remediation with human approval flows.
technical_design: Ops Weave is a thin orchestration layer that composes three primitives: Stitches (idempotent CLI/HTTP actions), Looms (typed parameter schemas + validation + dry-run simulation), and Safety Mesh (RBAC checks, rate limiters, circuit breakers). Stitches expose a small shim interface (stdin/stdout JSON or REST) and register metadata (cost estimate, affected resources, perms). Looms provide typed inputs, preflight validators (static checks + query of runtime telemetry), and can execute in dry-run mode producing a delta preview. Safety Mesh enforces permission escalation rules, automatic rollback hooks, and audit-log annotation. The runtime will run as an internal service with a GRPC control plane for the Console and a lightweight sidecar for Dedicated/Private deployments. We will reuse the admin-telemetry pipeline (ENG-151515) for execution metrics and the runbook provenance schema from ENG-824468.
acceptance_criteria: Engineers can register a new Stitch via CLI or manifest and run it in dry-run mode producing a JSON preview
Runbooks composed from Stitches enforce RBAC policy and require an approval step when safety rules trigger
Console shows per-stitch token-cost and latency estimates in the runbook composer
Weave records execution provenance and links back to the originating runbook/PR in audit logs
Automated fallback mode: if a Stitch fails 2x, Safety Mesh prevents auto-retry and surfaces a suggested remediation in the Console
migration_plan: Phase 1: introduce Stitches as a new package and migrate three high-value admin scripts to the shim (patch-rolling, quota-reset, and node-signal). Phase 2: onboard first responders and add Console composer integration. Phase 3: enable canary auto-remediation for low-risk playbooks. Each migration step includes a two-week dark launch and postmortem review. Rollbacks: toggles at workspace-level and ability to opt-out per-team. Backfills: migrate historical runbook metadata to provenance store via a one-off ETL job.
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: developer preview with internal SRE team; Week 3-4: invite CS/Support alpha; Week 5-8: Console integration and feature flag wide rollout; Week 9: enable telemetry-driven suggestion engine. Deploy to Hosted first, Dedicated beta next, Private on request. Monitor SLOs: runbook latency, success rate, and false-positive safety triggers.
